resources.string: Speaker, earpiece, headset, routes and volume
The audio service is missing: audioserver is not running or crashed at boot.
The audio policy exposes no output: the primary audio HAL did not load (check audioserver and vendor.audio-hal in logcat).
No wired or USB headset connected
A phone should expose speaker and earpiece: the device port is missing from audio_policy_configuration.xml (attachedDevices) or the HAL failed to open it.
%1$s Hz, %2$s frames per buffer, %3$d audio properties
PROPERTY_OUTPUT_SAMPLE_RATE is missing: the primary output did not open.
Unusual output sample rate %1$d Hz: check the mixPort profiles in the audio policy.
PROPERTY_OUTPUT_FRAMES_PER_BUFFER is missing: the primary output did not open.
The primary buffer is %1$s ms long: the fast/low-latency output is probably not configured.
SELinux does not let apps list /vendor/etc: check the files from adb.
No audio_policy_configuration.xml found: audioserver falls back to a default policy without the device routes.
No mixer_paths*.xml found: fine for non-Qualcomm HALs, on Qualcomm the HAL cannot set up any route.
The audio mode is %1$s with no call: a call or VoIP app did not release it, so routing follows the call path.
A stream has maximum volume 0: the volume curves of the audio policy are broken.
Media volume is 0 or muted: the interactive tests will be silent.
Skipped: audio mode is %1$s (call in progress)
AudioManager did not switch to IN_COMMUNICATION (mode stayed %1$s).
setCommunicationDevice(earpiece) was refused: the earpiece is not a valid communication device in the audio policy.
AudioFlinger refused the track: no output profile for this usage in audio_policy_configuration.xml, or the HAL failed to open the output stream.
The audio HAL does not consume data: its write() blocks, typical of a dead ADSP / ALSA path or a pcm_open that hangs. Check logcat for audio_hw_primary, msm-pcm, q6asm or adsp errors.
%1$d ms consumed, routed to %2$s, first frame after %3$d ms
getRoutedDevice() is empty: the policy did not report which device the track plays on.
Routed to %1$s instead of %2$s: the audio policy ignored the preferred device (check the route of this output in audio_policy_configuration.xml).
Data consumed at %1$d frames/s instead of %2$d: underruns or a wrong clock in the HAL / codec.

No AudioTimestamp: the HAL does not report a presentation position. On Qualcomm HALs this happens when pcm_open failed and the HAL sleeps instead of writing: listen to the output and check logcat for pcm errors.
AudioTimestamp stuck at frame %1$s: the HAL reports a position that does not advance.
Pick an output and a signal, then listen
Earpiece: the phone switches to VoIP mode while playing. Hold it to your ear.
The signal is not playing on the selected output: the audio policy chose another device.
The system refused the volume change.
Plug and unplug headphones: the check passes by itself when the event arrives.
Play a signal above, then answer
On the speaker the tone is clear and loud, without buzzing.
On the earpiece the tone is clearly audible with the phone at your ear.
With “Left only” the sound comes only from the left earphone.
With “Right only” the sound comes only from the right earphone.
A Bluetooth headset or speaker plays the signal without dropouts.
At maximum volume the music-like signal has no crackling or distortion.
